title: Interactive and Experiential Art
answer: Audience-reactive installations, generative AR and VR, dialogue engines, data sculptures and audio-visual systems.

children.name: Audience-Reactive Installations
children.blurb: Audience-reactive installations are artworks that change in real time based on the presence, movement, sound, or other signals from people in the space.

sections.body: Interactive and experiential art uses artificial intelligence to make work that changes in response to people, spaces, or data. In practice this means installations that track movement or sound and alter light, projection, or mechanical parts in real time. It also includes generative AR and VR scenes that build themselves as a visitor moves, dialogue engines that act as guides or characters, data sculptures that turn numbers into physical or projected shapes, and audio-visual systems that generate sound and image together. The work is not a simulation of intelligence but a set of responsive systems that read simple inputs and produce immediate output. Many pieces rely on computer vision, speech recognition, and generative models, but the models are usually small and tuned for a single room or event.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has solved basic real-time response, with cameras and microphones reliably detecting presence, motion, and loudness and mapping those signals to lights, motors, or projections without noticeable delay. What remains unsolved is longer-term coherence, since installations rarely remember a visitor across minutes or days and dialogue engines often break on unexpected questions. Generative AR and VR can produce novel scenery but struggle with stable physics, persistent objects, and consistent lighting. Data sculptures are expressive but usually require an artist to choose which data to show and how to shape it, and audio-visual systems can stay in sync for short loops but drift or repeat when left running. This site currently tracks no live image generation models, no video models, no audio models, and no AI tools, so the pages describe practices and examples rather than a current product directory.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Audience-Reactive Installations is the entry point for work that changes with visitors, and Generative AR and VR Environments extends that idea into headset and phone based spaces. Dialogue Engines and Virtual Docents covers conversational guides and characters, which often appear inside the installations or environments described in the first two pages. Data Sculpture turns information into physical or projected form, and it frequently draws on the same sensor data used by audience-reactive pieces. Audio-Visual Systems ties sound and image together, and its output often feeds the other four pages or stands alone as a performance. A reader would start with Audience-Reactive Installations for the core loop of sensing and response, then move to Generative AR and VR Environments for spatial work, Dialogue Engines and Virtual Docents for language, Data Sculpture for physical form, and Audio-Visual Systems for combined media.
